prompt: Make the jump feel forgiving: add 0.1 s of coyote time and a 0.1 s jump buffer.

config.plan_model: Agent-tool model parameter 'sonnet' (Claude Code sub-agent; the harness did not report the resolved model id)
config.how: one fresh general-purpose sub-agent per plan, reads a job file with project brief + the developer prompt, writes numbered plan (<=8 steps, no code) via Write; not Claude Code plan mode

plans.text:
1. Read player.gd to learn how movement, gravity, jump input, and is_on_floor() are currently handled, and note which physics callback drives them.
2. Define two tunable values, coyote time and jump buffer time, both defaulting to 0.1 s, as exported variables so they can be tweaked in the editor without touching logic.
3. Add a coyote timer that resets to full while the player is on the floor and counts down once they leave it, and make sure a jump that walks off a ledge is not counted as a coyote window.
4. Add a jump-buffer timer that is set to full whenever the jump button is pressed and counts down every physics frame.
5. Replace the direct "on floor and jump pressed" check with a combined rule: jump if the buffer timer is active and the coyote timer is active.
6. When a jump fires, immediately zero both timers so a single press cannot trigger a double jump, and keep variable-height jump (early release) behavior intact.
7. Check that the existing animation, sprite flipping, and enemy stomp or bounce logic still work, since they may rely on floor state or jump velocity.
8. Playtest in level_01.tscn: jump just after leaving a platform edge, press jump just before landing, and confirm normal jumps, double-jump prevention, and the 0.1 s feel are correct, then adjust values if needed.

1. Read player.gd to learn how movement, gravity, the jump input, and is_on_floor checks are currently handled, and note which input action name triggers a jump.
2. Add two tunable values at the top of the script, a coyote time and a jump buffer time, both defaulting to 0.1 s, exposed as exports so they can be tweaked in the editor without touching logic.
3. Add two countdown timers as plain variables: one for remaining coyote time and one for remaining buffer time, so no extra nodes need to be added to the scene tree.
4. Each physics frame, reset the coyote countdown to its full value while the player is on the floor, and otherwise decrement it toward zero using the frame delta.
5. When the jump action is pressed, set the buffer countdown to its full value instead of jumping immediately, and decrement it each frame otherwise.
6. Perform the jump when the buffer countdown is above zero and the coyote countdown is above zero, then zero both so a single press cannot trigger a double jump or a second jump in the air.
7. Make sure a ledge walk-off does not refresh the coyote window after jumping, and keep any existing variable-height jump cut (releasing the button early) working with the new flow.
8. Playtest in level_01.tscn: jump just after leaving a platform edge, press jump slightly before landing, and confirm normal jumps, enemy interactions, and double-jump prevention all still behave correctly, then tune the 0.1 s values if needed.

1. Read player.gd to learn how movement, gravity, is_on_floor checks, and the jump input are currently handled. Note the existing jump velocity, input action name, and where physics processing happens.
2. Add two tunable values at the top of the script, a coyote time of 0.1 s and a jump buffer time of 0.1 s, exposed as exported variables so they can be tweaked in the editor.
3. Add two countdown timers as plain float variables (one for time since leaving the ground, one for time since jump was pressed) rather than Timer nodes, keeping the scene tree unchanged.
4. Each physics frame, reset the coyote counter to full while the player is on the floor and decrement it by delta otherwise. Also decrement the jump buffer counter by delta, clamped at zero.
5. When the jump action is pressed, set the jump buffer counter to its full value instead of jumping immediately.
6. Perform the jump when the buffer counter is above zero and the coyote counter is above zero, then zero both counters so one press cannot trigger a double jump.
7. Make sure a jump that began from coyote time does not let the player jump again in mid-air, and that variable-height jump release (if present) still works with the new flow.
8. Playtest in level_01.tscn by walking off ledges and pressing jump slightly late, and pressing jump slightly before landing, then tune the two values and check that enemy-stomp bounces and other code paths that set velocity are unaffected.

2. Add two tunable constants (or exported variables) for coyote time and jump buffer time, both defaulting to 0.1 s, so they can be adjusted in the editor without touching logic.
3. Add two countdown timers as plain variables in player.gd: one for coyote time, one for the jump buffer, updated every physics frame using the delta value.
4. Each physics frame, reset the coyote counter to full while the player is on the floor, and otherwise let it tick down toward zero.
5. When the jump button is pressed, set the buffer counter to full; otherwise let it tick down toward zero.
6. Trigger a jump when the buffer counter is above zero and the coyote counter is above zero, then zero both counters immediately so a single press cannot cause a double jump or a jump after leaving the ground twice.
7. Make sure a jump that begins from a jump press cancels the coyote window, and that any existing variable-height or release-to-shorten jump logic still works with the new trigger condition.
8. Playtest in level_01.tscn: walk off ledges and press jump just after, press jump just before landing, and confirm normal jumps, enemy interactions, and double-jump prevention are unchanged; then tune the two values if needed.

1. Read player.gd to learn how movement, gravity, jump input, and is_on_floor() are currently handled, and note any existing jump-related variables or input action names.
2. Check the Input Map for the jump action so the buffer listens to the right action, and confirm how variable jump height or double jumps (if any) interact with jumping.
3. Add two exported tuning values, coyote time and jump buffer time, both defaulting to 0.1 s, so they can be tweaked in the Inspector without editing the script.
4. Add two countdown timers (as script variables rather than Timer nodes) for the remaining coyote window and the remaining buffer window, updated every physics frame using delta.
5. Reset the coyote countdown to full whenever the player is on the floor, and let it tick down once airborne; reset the buffer countdown to full whenever the jump button is pressed.
6. Change the jump condition so the player jumps when the buffer is active and either on the floor or inside the coyote window; on jumping, zero both countdowns so a single press cannot trigger a double jump.
7. Make sure a jump press while airborne past the coyote window does not trigger, and that walking off a ledge after jumping does not grant a free extra jump.
8. Playtest in level_01.tscn by walking off ledges and pressing jump slightly late, and by pressing jump just before landing, then adjust the values or edge cases as needed.
